| D0136 | A | `lineage` classifies every atom it cannot resolve, and propagates the one error that is not a resolution failure | docs/specs/m2.md §7 requires `lineage` to be TOTAL: "an atom that does not resolve is classified, never raised on". Totality has to be given a boundary, because `Store.get_value` can fail three ways and they are not the same failure. . CLASSIFIED as `kind="unresolved"`: (1) `MissingRef` — nothing is stored at that ref. This is the case §7 names, and §6's absence witness is why it is not hypothetical: an anti-join cites a relation's content address and nothing guarantees that relation was ever stored. (2) `CanonicalEncodingError` — bytes are stored, and they are not a value. `Store.put_bytes` legitimately holds raw bytes (a source's own bytes are stored that way), so a ref can address something real that is nevertheless not a `srcrow/1` and not a `rel/1` and not anything else with a decodable canonical form. The taxonomy has three kinds and none of them is "bytes I cannot read", so this is the honest one: nothing here resolves to a value lineage can describe. . PROPAGATED: `IntegrityError` — bytes at rest that no longer hash to the ref they are filed under. This is not a citation failing to resolve; it is the store reporting that its own contract has been broken, which `Store.get_bytes` verifies on every read precisely so it can be noticed. Classifying it as `"unresolved"` would launder detected tampering into "not found" inside the one read a reader is most likely to trust — a serve-layer lineage view — and would make the store's verify-on-read pointless exactly where it matters most. A lineage read that raises here is a lineage read that has found something no caller can handle by carrying on. . The narrow reading of "total" — never raises, ever — was considered and rejected for that reason. Totality here is a property of the CITATION (every atom gets a classification), not a promise that the storage layer underneath is functioning. . A fourth kind for a malformed atom is not needed and is not added: `Why.of` refuses a non-ref by name, so a malformed atom cannot reach a `Rel` and therefore cannot reach here (L2.7 checks that rather than asserting it). | accepted | — | — | pytest: `tests/laws/m2/test_l2_lineage.py::test_l2_7_an_atom_that_is_not_in_the_store_is_classified_not_raised_on`; pytest: `tests/laws/m2/test_l2_lineage.py::test_l2_7_an_atom_outside_the_pinned_grammar_is_unconstructible`; file: `src/tannen/sources.py` |

| D0146 | A | Two ways an ad-hoc run leaks into a guarded one: an inherited TANNEN_ variable (fixed) and a .pyc in a sealed directory (queued, because the guard that catches it is the trust root) | Both were found the same way — by running commands against this repo during the M2 sitting-materials pass and watching guards report failures that were mine rather than the code's. Both are the same family: ambient process state reaching into a run that believes it controls its own conditions. One is fixed here; one is queued, with its mitigation written down. . (1) FIXED — `tests/test_laws_runner.py` inherited the environment it meant to override. `run_pytest` built its child env as `dict(os.environ, TANNEN_EVIDENCE_ROOT=…)`: inherit everything, override one. An ambient `TANNEN_NO_EVIDENCE=1` — exactly what someone sets so an ad-hoc run does not dirty `evidence/` — rode into the child, the plugin wrote nothing, and FOUR tests failed asserting records that were never going to exist. Every one of those failures names the harness, so they read as a regression in it while the cause is outside the process entirely. Observed, not hypothesised: it cost a round trip during this session. . The cure is the one this repo already owns for a different family. `scripts/_gov.py`'s `git_env()` strips `GIT_LOCATION_VARS` because `GIT_DIR` beats `git -C`, and the rule it encodes is: SCRUB THE FAMILY, THEN SET EXACTLY WHAT YOU MEAN. `child_env()` now does that for `TANNEN_EVIDENCE_ROOT`, `TANNEN_NO_EVIDENCE` and `TANNEN_CHECK_DECISIONS_NESTED`, at all three sites that spawn a pytest subprocess — including the two that deliberately SET one of them, because a test that says what it needs must not also inherit the negation. . `test_the_harness_scrubs_an_ambient_tannen_variable` constructs the hostile state (D0092): it sets the variable in its own process for the duration rather than trusting nobody will. Watched failing against the inheriting spelling and passing against the scrub. . THE GATE WAS NEVER SILENTLY WEAKENED BY THIS, which is worth stating so the fix is not read as larger than it is: with `TANNEN_NO_EVIDENCE=1` ambient, `make verify`'s pytest writes nothing and the very next step, `tannen laws report`, fails on missing evidence. It fails loudly. The damage was confined to spurious failures in one test file. . (2) QUEUED — `scripts/custodian.sh:66` and `scripts/check_manifest.py:113` disagree about `__pycache__`. The custodian enumerates `$(find tests/poison -type f | sort)` and requires a manifest row for every result, with no exclusion; `check_manifest.check_sealed_paths` skips any path with `__pycache__` in its parts, by name. So a `.pyc` written into `tests/poison/oracle-shadow/` — which happens on any import from that directory without `-B` or `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` — leaves `check_manifest` green and the custodian red. Reproduced: this session's own manual runs of the oracle-shadow reproduction did exactly that, and `make verify` failed at its LAST step after 37 minutes with "custodian: FAIL — not manifested: …/bootstrap_shadow.cpython-313-pytest-9.1.1.pyc". . THE MESSAGE INVITES THE WRONG FIX, and that is what makes it worth recording rather than just cleaning up. "not manifested: <path>" reads as "add a manifest row", and a manifest row for a `.pyc` would be wrong twice over: the file is gitignored, and its name carries the interpreter version, so the row would break on the next Python. The only correct response is to delete the file, which the message does not say. . NOT FIXED HERE because `scripts/custodian.sh` is the trust root and author-key territory (CLAUDE.md hard rules, BRIEF §9.1): only the owner edits it. Queued for M3 rather than added to the M2 driver, which is already 1468 lines and whose step 6 would need a newly tuned custodian copy for a one-line exclusion. THE MITIGATION IS FREE AND IS WRITTEN DOWN: every in-repo runner already does the right thing — `tests/test_governance_scripts.py`'s poison matrix sets `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` and its oracle-shadow tests pass `-B` — so the hazard is reachable only from ad-hoc commands. Do not import from `tests/poison/` without `-B`. . ONE THING THE SITTING SHOULD KNOW: the driver's `unexpected_failures()` does NOT tolerate a "not manifested:" line, so if this debris is present when the owner starts, step 0's gate stops the sitting over a stray `.pyc`. `find tests/poison -name __pycache__ -type d` before running is a five-second precaution. | accepted | — | governance-paths | pytest: `tests/test_laws_runner.py::test_the_harness_scrubs_an_ambient_tannen_variable`; file: `tests/test_laws_runner.py`; manifest: `scripts/custodian.sh` |
| D0147 | A | Three defects in the M2 sitting driver that only executing it could find: a binding orphaned by the fixture it names, a guard patch that reddens a test file it never mentions, and a projection left stale by the two steps that run after it | The M2 driver was read closely, step by step, and every new step was applied in a sandbox and watched refusing a second application (D0143). All three defects below survived all of that and were found by rehearsing the finished driver end to end — one per run, each deeper than the last, because a rehearsal only tests as far as it gets. None is exotic; all three are the same shape — a step's blast radius reaching past the file it edits, to a file it does not name. . (1) A BINDING THAT NAMED THE FIXTURE'S CANDIDATE PATH DIED WHEN STEP 5 MOVED IT. Found by the first rehearsal, which exited 1 at step 5 with ten failed post-conditions. D0141 binds `docs/redteam/fixture-candidates/oracle-shadow-model/README.md`. Step 5 `git mv`s that directory into `tests/poison/`, and the driver's own post-move guard — written for exactly this, twenty lines below the move — stopped the sitting with "a decision binding stopped resolving when the fixtures moved". The guard was right. The sitting stopping was not: the repair is mechanical, it is builder work, and it belongs in the same breath as the move that causes it rather than in the owner's lap five steps in. . FIXED BY RETARGETING, NOT DROPPING. At M1 the same shape was answered by deleting the binding before the sitting (D0104's note, quoted in step 5b). That is a real answer and a lossy one: `tests/poison/` is sealed and manifested, so a binding on the installed path still names a file whose removal turns `check_manifest` red, where a dropped binding names nothing. Step 5 now retargets it, correcting the `detail`'s tense in the same replacement — "staged outside tests/poison/" stops being true the instant the `git mv` lands, and a true future tense left standing becomes a false present one, which is the correction step 4h makes to D0110 for the same reason. Guarded on the directory AND on the old path still being present, so it is inert on a resumed sitting and on a declined install. . THIS IS BUILDER WORK BECAUSE OF A FACT ABOUT D0141 SPECIFICALLY, not a general licence: it is Tier A and unsigned. Were it Tier C and signed, D0063 ruling 2 would make its bindings as immutable as its text and the edit and the re-signature would have to be one act — the shape step 4h uses. . (2) STEP 4g'S GUARD PATCH TURNS FOUR CASES OF A TEST FILE IT NEVER MENTIONS RED. Found by the same run, as two of the four violations at step 5's post-move check. `tests/test_tier_c_signatures.py` is hermetic: it builds a throwaway tree and writes a `DECISIONS.md` that is a bare `input_hash` header, with a comment saying projection freshness is not what those tests are about. RT-M2-05's fix gives the projection a SECOND thing it must carry — the attention-receipt line the run computes, because the hash cannot see the clock — so a bare header stopped being a fresh projection the moment the patch landed. Four of the file's seven cases assert exit 0; all four went red. D0063 and D0064 both bind that file, which is how the rehearsal surfaced it. . Left as drafted, step 4g would have closed the M2 boundary on a red suite — the gate at step 9 would have failed, after five signatures and a receipt. . THE FIXTURE IS CORRECTED IN THE SAME EDIT, from `receipt_state` — the function the guard itself calls — so a throwaway tree with no `receipts/` states the STALE verdict it actually has rather than faking a FRESH one. The alternative, letting the guard pass when the projection carries no receipt line at all, was rejected: it reopens the hole RT-M2-05 named, since `DECISIONS.md`'s own bytes are not an input to the hash that guards it, so deleting the line would become the evasion. `tests/test_tier_c_signatures.py` is neither frozen nor custody-set, so it needs no signature; it lands beside the guard because landing it separately means landing it red. Same shape as step 4f (the Makefile and its docstring) and step 4i (the schema, the check and the test). . (3) THE PROJECTION IS STALE AT THE CLOSING GATE, BECAUSE BOTH OF ITS CLOCK-DEPENDENT INPUTS ARRIVE AFTER THE LAST STEP THAT REGENERATED IT. Found by the third rehearsal, the first to survive far enough to reach the close: eight post-conditions green — receipt taken and signed, `m2-close` minted and verifying as `owner@tannen`, custody set signed, custodian green with no tolerances — and then step 11's `make verify` red, with "DECISIONS.md's attention-receipt line is not what today computes". `DECISIONS.md` was last generated at the top of step 9. Step 9's custodian then writes `receipts/<today>.md` and step 10 mints the close tag, and BOTH are inputs to the freshness verdict, so the projection asserts the PREVIOUS boundary's window while the run computes this one's. The second violation in that gate — `tests/test_governance_scripts.py` — was a cascade of the first, since that file runs `check_decisions` against the real tree. . THIS IS RT-M2-05'S OWN FINDING, REAPPEARING INSIDE THE DRIVER THAT FIXES IT, and that is the argument for the fix rather than an irony. Before step 4g's check existed nothing could say the projection was stale, so every prior sitting simply carried the staleness into its closing commit — which is precisely the state the red team found in the tree M1 left behind. The new check found it on its first outing, in the one place the builder had not thought to look. . FIXED BY REGENERATING IN STEP 11, immediately before the closing gate, because there is no earlier point at which both inputs exist. Neither `DECISIONS.md` nor `CONCEPTS.md` is in `MANIFEST.sha256` or in the custody set — checked against both files, not assumed — so the regeneration disturbs no seal and invalidates no signature, and step 11's own commit picks the result up. The alternative of regenerating after the sitting was rejected because it is what was already nominally true and what failed: `docs/SITTING.md` listed "regenerate the projections" under work for the builder afterwards, which means the boundary commit is sealed and tagged around a projection known to be wrong. That line is the habit that caused this, and it has been removed. . VERIFIED FROM THE FAILING SIDE, all three items, per `produce-the-failure`. (1) was watched stopping a rehearsal, and the corrected step was watched applying its diff and the same check then passing on to step 5b in a live run. (2) was reproduced locally in the order that proves it: guard patched and fixture NOT -> 4 failed / 3 passed, each failure naming the missing attention-receipt line; fixture patched -> 7 passed. The guard itself was then checked both ways on the real tree — exit 0 today, and exit 1 at `--today 2026-09-08` with four violations naming the header and D0006/D0014/D0020, which is precisely what step 4g's own note text promises. (3) was reproduced in the rehearsal clone kept frozen in the state the failure left it: `check_decisions` red on the attention-receipt line, then `gen_projections.py`, then `check_decisions: OK — 146 records valid, DECISIONS.md fresh`. That clone's full `make verify` was then run to completion — green end to end, 716 passed / 1 skipped / 1 xfailed, custodian green, custody floor intact — which is what establishes that the second violation was a cascade of the first and not a separate defect. . NOT A DEFECT, AND WORTH KNOWING BEFORE THE NEXT RUN: step 5's post-move check reports two violations mid-sitting — a stale `DECISIONS.md` (step 4 edited decision records, so the input hash has legitimately moved and step 9 regenerates) and `tests/test_governance_scripts.py` failing on the dirty tree. Two is the expected noise at that point. | D0148 | A | D0147's item 3 names the wrong input, and the decline path's stop is the guard working: what rehearsing the M2 driver from a clean HEAD corrected | The `--from head --answers n` rehearsal — the first run ever to enter the driver with a clean tree — corrected one claim in D0147 and settled two questions about the decline path. This is a NEW record rather than an edit to D0147 because D0045 makes a decision's fields immutable and no guard enforces that; the record of the mistake is part of the record. . (1) THE CORRECTION. D0147 item 3 says the projection is stale at the closing gate because "BOTH of the projection's clock-dependent inputs arrived after it", and that `DECISIONS.md` "was last generated at the top of step 9". Both halves are wrong, and in the same way: step 9 regenerates TWICE. `gen_projections.py` runs at its top (`boundary_sitting.sh:1817`) and `make digest` runs at its end (`:1822`), after `custodian.sh` has written and signed `receipts/<today>.md`. So the receipt IS accounted for by the time step 9 ends. THE CLOSE TAG IS THE SOLE INPUT THAT ARRIVES AFTER THE LAST REGENERATION, minted by step 10. . THE EVIDENCE IS A CLONE STOPPED IN EXACTLY THAT STATE. The decline run halted at step 10 with the receipt written and signed, `make digest` run, and no close tag; its `DECISIONS.md:10` reads "receipt 2026-09-01.md fresh (no milestone boundary since)". `_gov.py:300-306` takes that branch when no boundary tag is dated on or after the receipt, and the "fresh until <d+7> (boundary <d> + 7d)" branch once one is — and the latter string, naming 2026-09-01, is precisely what the third rehearsal's step-11 failure quoted as what today computes. One input, not two. . THE FIX D0147 DESCRIBES IS UNCHANGED AND THIS SHARPENS ITS ARGUMENT rather than weakening it. Step 11's regeneration is not merely the earliest convenient point; it is the first opportunity after the only missing input exists, since the tag is minted at step 10 and step 11 is the next step. What is now known to be unnecessary is any worry about the receipt: D0147's "no earlier point where both inputs exist" reasoning arrives at the right placement for a reason that is half wrong, and a future reader moving that regeneration earlier on the strength of it would break the fix. Hence this record. . (2) THE COVERAGE GAP IS CLOSED. `--from worktree` can never reach `RESUMED=0` — the harness dirties four tracked files before the driver starts — so until this run, step 0's precondition gate and the RT-M2-06 D1 `else` branch had never executed in any rehearsal, including the green one banked before the seven new steps. This run entered with a clean tree: no "so this is a RESUMED sitting" note, no stray-dirt note, the gate offered and declined. The branch that decides resumption from sitting-shaped artifacts only, rather than from any dirt at all, is now exercised rather than reasoned about. . (3) THE DECLINE PATH IS NOT CHEAP, AND THE PLAN SAID IT WOULD BE. It took 3522 seconds — 59 minutes — because declining step 0's gate does not avoid step 9's, which is not behind a `confirm` (`:1819`). Neither are the regeneration, the custodian, or the digest; only the commit is. A decline run therefore costs about what an accept run costs, and the reason to run one is coverage, never speed. . (4) ITS STOP IS THE GUARD WORKING, NOT A FOURTH DEFECT. Because step 9's writes are unconditional and its commit is not, answering `n` throughout leaves a modified `DECISIONS.md` and an untracked signed receipt and digest. Step 10 then refuses: "the tree is not clean, so m2-close would attest a commit that does not contain this sitting's work — and would quote working-tree hashes absent from it (D0051)". That is exactly the property RT-M2-06 D2 was written to restore, firing correctly, before any tag was signed. The harness's two failed checks — "ran to completion" and "no step aborted" — are accept-path expectations that do not apply to a full decline, and the run is read as green on the question it was launched to answer. . (5) OBSERVED AND DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED BEFORE THE SITTING: a declined sitting is not a no-op. `custodian.sh` writes and signs the receipt before the owner is asked to commit anything, so abandoning a decline leaves a signed receipt untracked — and step 0 clause (b) reads untracked `receipts/` as sitting artifacts, making the NEXT run `RESUMED=1` and skipping the precondition gate. Every part of that is correct on its own terms: a receipt does exist, and the resumed branch announces itself rather than acting silently. It is recorded because "I ran it and declined everything" leaves state behind, which is not what a reader would assume, and because moving the receipt behind a confirm is a change to the order the receipt-then-tag argument depends on (D0071) — not something to attempt six days before the deadline, on the strength of a path the owner will not take. | accepted | — | governance-paths | file: `decisions/0147-three-defects-only-running-the-driver-could-find.yaml`; file: `docs/proposals/2026-08-31-m2-boundary-sitting/boundary_sitting.sh`; file: `scripts/_gov.py`; file: `scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh` |
| D0149 | A | The rehearsal verdict read the clock twice and called a signed receipt missing: a midnight-crossing defect in the harness, not the driver | `scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh` asserted the sitting's attention receipt by recomputing the date at verdict time — `test -f "$CLONE/receipts/$(date +%F).md"` and the matching `.sig`. That is a SECOND reading of a clock the driver already read, hours earlier, inside `custodian.sh`. Replaced both checks with a snapshot-and-difference: capture the clone's receipts before the driver starts (`RECEIPTS_BEFORE`, taken beside `CLOSE_TAG_PREEXISTED`) and let the verdict ask which receipt THIS RUN ADDED. . WHAT IT COST TO FIND. The `--from head --answers y` rehearsal began 2026-09-01 21:36 and its custodian wrote and signed `receipts/2026-09-01.md` at 23:23. The verdict ran after midnight, computed `2026-09-02`, and printed FAIL twice — "this sitting took a fresh attention receipt" and "and signed it" — against a clone where both were true and the files were sitting on disk, signed, committed, and covered by a green custodian run. . THIS IS THE HARNESS, NOT THE DRIVER, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE POINT. The driver ran to completion (exit 0), aborted no step, minted `m2-close` and verified it as owner@tannen, signed the custody set, and left the custodian green with no tolerances. Nothing about the sitting it rehearsed was wrong. So this defect does NOT invalidate the driver evidence from runs 4 and 5, and does not trigger the "re-run all three paths" rule that a DRIVER edit triggers — that rule exists because a run stops at its first failure, and no run stopped here. . THE REAL SITTING WAS NEVER AT RISK, and it is worth saying why rather than assuming it. `date +%F` appeared exactly twice in the harness and nowhere in the driver's assertions: `custodian.sh` names the receipt once, and everything downstream — `check_receipts.py`, `receipt_state` in `_gov.py` — reads the LATEST receipt off the directory rather than recomputing a name. An owner sitting that crosses midnight therefore behaves correctly; only the rehearsal's scorecard was wrong. . AND A SELF-INFLICTED ONE, RECORDED BECAUSE IT NEARLY COST THE EVIDENCE. This fix was applied to `rehearse_sitting.sh` WHILE run 5 was still executing that same file. `bash` reads a script incrementally by byte offset rather than parsing it whole, so inserting ten lines shifted every offset after them and the running shell resumed mid-construct: `rehearse_sitting.sh: line 326: syntax error near unexpected token '('`. The file was never invalid — `bash -n` passes on it — but the run died after its last check and before `say "Unexpected failure lines in the transcript"`, losing that section and the final tally. Both were recoverable ONLY because `--keep` had preserved the transcript, and were re-derived by running the harness's own awk program against it: one line, `check_decisions: FAIL (2 violation(s))` at step 5, which is the expected mid-sitting pair D0147 already documents as NOT a defect. THE RULE: never edit a shell script that is currently running. Copy it, edit the copy, and swap it in after the run exits. | accepted | — | governance-paths | file: `scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh`; file: `docs/proposals/2026-08-31-m2-boundary-sitting/boundary_sitting.sh` |
| D0150 | A | The branch that carries the owner's first command was the one branch never rehearsed: the harness erased the custody drift it was supposed to reproduce | `scripts/rehearse_sitting.sh` copied the driver under test into the clone's `scripts/boundary_sitting.sh` and only AFTERWARDS ran `gen_custody.py` and re-signed `governance/custody.sha256`. Because that path is a custody-set member, regenerating after the copy folded the new driver's bytes into the custody set — so the clone had no drift, step 0's gate was green, and the branch that tolerates the drift never executed. The `cp` is now DEFERRED until after the custody set is generated and signed, which reproduces the owner's real starting state in both modes. . WHAT THE OWNER ACTUALLY DOES, AND WHY IT WAS UNTESTED. The sitting begins `cp docs/proposals/<…>/boundary_sitting.sh scripts/` against a custody set the owner signed at the LAST sitting, over the PREVIOUS milestone's driver. That copy is custody drift by construction: the gate is red from the owner's first command, and step 0 continues only because `unexpected_failures()` tolerates that one drift by name until step 7 re-signs. Six rehearsals passed without once running it — `grep -c "green except the custody set"` over all four kept transcripts returns 0. . THE TOLERANCE WAS THEN VERIFIED DIRECTLY, because a fix that assumes the branch works is the same mistake one layer up. The drift state was reproduced in the kept run-6 clone and the real guards were run against it: `check_manifest` emits `custody drift: scripts/boundary_sitting.sh changed since the custody file was written` under a `check_manifest: FAIL (1 violation(s))` header, and the custodian emits `custody set hashes do not verify` and `custody floor violated`. Feeding that captured output to the driver's own `unexpected_failures()` returns EMPTY, so step 0 prints "green except the custody set, which is this sitting's step 7 — continuing". The branch is correct. It had simply never been executed, which is a different fact and the one worth fixing. . ORDERING CONSTRAINT, since two properties compete. The copy must land AFTER the custody signing (or there is no drift to rehearse) and BEFORE head mode's fixture commit (or the copy is uncommitted, the tree is dirty, and `RESUMED=0` — the branch D0148 bought — is lost again). The single insertion point that satisfies both is between them. . `docs/SITTING.md` carried the matching documentation defect and is corrected in the same pass: its driver line read `bash scripts/boundary_sitting.sh [milestone]` with no `cp`, while `scripts/boundary_sitting.sh` holds the M1 driver — a 1216-line divergence that a driver would not announce, because it takes its milestone from the argument. . AND THE FIX IS VERIFIABLE FROM ONLY ONE MODE, which is worth stating because getting it wrong cost a run. | D0152 | A | Everything the M2 sitting's machinery got wrong, and why every fix is the owner's | The M2 boundary sitting completed on 2026-09-03 and exposed six defects in the machinery that ran it. The title does not count them because the count kept moving while this record was being written; item 6 is the one that matters most and was found last, by reading the gate's own passing output. Editing any of them breaks the owner's signature over `governance/custody.sha256`, so each fix is a Tier-C door the builder may not open. That warning is written for a FRESH sitting, where the binding really is unresolved. On a resumed one the binding already resolves — `check_decisions` reported `0 unenforced` throughout — so declining is correct and nothing downstream stops. The fix is to test the POST-state (does the record name the installed path?) rather than the pre-state, which is the shape the step's own neighbours use. . AND THE TRIGGER PHRASE IS DELIBERATELY LEFT IN PLACE. D0141's binding detail is builder-landable, so rewording "retargeted from docs/redteam/fixture-candidates/…" would disarm this guard today at no cost. It is not reworded, for two reasons: the sentence is true and is the only surviving record of where that fixture came from, and removing it would falsify this record's own evidence while leaving the defect exactly where it is. A workaround that makes the bug unreproducible is worse than the bug. . ITEM 2 — STEP 4f'S SKIP-GUARD TESTS ONE OF THE THREE FILES ITS DECLINE BRANCH REVERTS. The guard is `boundary_sitting.sh:694`, `grep -q 'scripts/check_laws.py' Makefile`. The decline branch is `:786`, `git checkout -- Makefile .github/workflows/ci.yml tests/test_law_validation.py`. The set the guard reads is a strict subset of the set the revert writes, so any state where the Makefile is edited and the other two are not reads as "already in the Makefile — skipped" and the step never runs again. That state is reachable, and was reached (D0153): `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is today byte-identical to `docs/proposals/2026-08-25-boundary-sitting/ci.yml`, so step 4b's `diff -q` guard skips it too and no gate anywhere can see the gap. . What was actually lost is a comment. `ci.yml`'s whole job is `- run: make verify`, and the file has never executed — the repo has no remote, as its own header says. The effect is cosmetic; the shape is not. A guard that reads a subset of what it writes is the same class this project has now filed four times (D0071, D0091, D0149, and item 1 above): a check whose answer cannot depend on what it claims to check. . ITEM 3 — `custodian.sh:283-284` SIGNS THE ATTENTION RECEIPT WITHOUT CHECKING THE EXIT STATUS, and `:285` then prints "attention receipt written and author-signed" regardless. A failed `ssh-keygen -Y sign` — a locked agent, a missing key file, a declined touch on the hardware-backed owner key — produces a receipt with no `.sig` and a success line saying otherwise. The next `make verify` would catch it at `check_receipts` ("latest receipt is unsigned"), so this is not silent for ever; it is silent at the one moment the owner is standing there able to retry, and it fails in the direction of appearing to have worked. The receipt is the sole artifact the Tier-B silence-as-consent clock rests on (`_gov.py` `receipt_state`), which is why this is filed rather than shrugged at. Queue it beside D0146 item 2's missing `__pycache__` exclusion — same file, same sitting. . ITEM 4 — THE DRIVER HAS NO LOCK. The sitting is a single-run ceremony by construction and nothing in the driver says so. Two concurrent runs against one worktree produced item 2 and a duplicate attention receipt (D0153). A `flock` on a lockfile beside the transcript, refusing to start while another run holds it, is a few lines and removes the entire class. . ITEM 5 — THE INSTALLED FIXTURE'S OWN README STILL DESCRIBES IT AS STAGED AND UNPATCHED. `tests/poison/oracle-shadow-model/README.md` opens "**needs patch** — … Against the shipped check this fixture does not bite, which is why it is staged here and not in `tests/poison/`", and its reproduction command still names `PYTHONPATH=docs/redteam/fixture-candidates/oracle-shadow-model`, a path the sitting's own `git mv` deleted. Every clause is now false: D0142 replaced the two hardcoded name constants with `_frozen_oracles()`, which derives the map from `tests/laws/m*/_*.py` off the filesystem, and the fixture bites (see D0141's upgraded binding). The file is custody set, so the correction is the owner's; the staging-side copy at `docs/redteam/fixture-candidates/README.md`, which is neither frozen nor custody, is corrected by the builder in the same change as this record. . ITEM 6 — THE CUSTODIAN NEVER RUNS THE FIXTURE THIS SITTING INSTALLED, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL. `tests/poison/oracle-shadow-model/` closes RT-M2-01, the M1->M2 pass's single CRITICAL finding. The sitting `git mv`d it into the sealed corpus, wrote its three `MANIFEST.sha256` rows, wrote its three `governance/custody.sha256` rows, and added its row to `tests/poison/README.md`'s table. It did NOT add the fourth thing the corpus's own installation recipe requires — a `poison` line in `scripts/custodian.sh`. Verified from the gate's passing output: the custodian prints sixteen "fails its poison as required" lines and none names oracle-shadow-model; `grep -c oracle-shadow-model scripts/custodian.sh` is 0. All thirteen other installed fixtures have their line. This one is the only gap. . WHY IT HAPPENED, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. Step 6 installs the custodian by comparing the live file against `$PROPOSALS_M1/custodian.sh` — the PREVIOUS milestone's draft — and its comment (`boundary_sitting.sh:1591-1592`) still reads "This sitting's own draft is the LIVE custodian.sh plus one new poison line for oracle-shadow (RT-M1-01)". That sentence was true at M1 and was carried into the M2 driver unchanged. `docs/proposals/2026-08-31-m2-boundary-sitting/` contains no `custodian.sh` at all, so there was no M2 draft to install: the comparison found the M1 draft already applied, printed "already applied — skipped", and the sitting proceeded. Nothing was declined and nothing failed; the step simply had nothing to offer. . THIS IS D0095'S SHAPE EXACTLY, ONE FILE OVER. `required_tags` lags because the session that mints a boundary tag may not edit the frozen file naming it required; the poison list lags because the sitting that installs a fixture installs a custodian drafted before that fixture existed. Both are hand-kept enumerations extended only at the moment their extender is least able to edit them. D0095's half (2) — "replace the enumeration with a rule that derives the required set" — is the fix both need, and the guard this sitting shipped shows it is achievable: D0142 replaced the oracle map's two hardcoded names with `_frozen_oracles()`, which reads `tests/laws/m*/_*.py` off the filesystem. A `poison` loop over `tests/poison/*/` that REFUSES a directory with no invocation would close this one the same way, and would have failed loudly on 2026-09-03 instead of finishing sooner. . WHAT IS AND IS NOT EXPOSED. The fixture is not unexercised: this change adds `tests/test_governance_scripts.py::test_oracle_shadow_model_fails_its_poison`, which runs it, and D0141's binding now points at that test. But `tests/test_governance_scripts.py` is neither frozen nor custody-set, so a builder may delete it and `custodian.sh` will still print "custody floor intact". The custody floor is the thing meant to hold when the builder is the adversary, and for this one fixture it currently does not. That is why this is item 6 and not a footnote to item 5. | accepted | — | governance-paths | file: `scripts/boundary_sitting.sh`; file: `scripts/custodian.sh`; manifest: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; file: `tests/poison/oracle-shadow-model/README.md` |

WHAT HAPPENED. Two invocations of `scripts/boundary_sitting.sh m2` were running against the same worktree at the same time, by accident. Both stopped at the same place — the D0141 retarget guard, D0152 item 1 — and both were killed by hand. The third run completed. . ARTIFACT 1 — A REVERTED FILE NO GATE CAN SEE. One run applied step 4f's edit to `Makefile`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `tests/test_law_validation.py`; the other was already past step 4f's guard, took a decline, and ran `git checkout --` over all three. Two were re-applied by the run that owned them; `ci.yml` was not, because the guard reads only the Makefile and now says "already — skipped". The lost bytes are a comment. The mechanism is D0152 item 2. . ARTIFACT 2 — TWO RECEIPTS AT ONE HEAD, AND A CHAIN LINE THAT VANISHED. `receipts/2026-09-02.md` and `receipts/2026-09-03.md` both record `HEAD: 14647976e9b447775f10049614898b764158d8ee`. Both are owner-signed and `check_receipts` accepts the pair, correctly: it requires each receipt's HEAD to be an ancestor of the next, and a commit is its own ancestor. The custodian overwrites `receipts/$(date +%F).md` unconditionally, so a re-run on a new day simply adds one. . The interesting half is what the second one is MISSING. `2026-09-02.md` carries "- previous receipt: 2026-08-31 at 64e0b155…"; `2026-09-03.md` carries no such line at all. `custodian.sh:268` computes `prev=$(ls -1 receipts/*.md | sort | tail -1)` and `:273` emits the line only `if [ "$prev" != "$receipt" ]`. The first run had already written `receipts/2026-09-03.md`, so the second run's `tail -1` returned the very file it was about to overwrite, the condition went false, and the chain line was dropped. THIS IS NOT COLLISION-SPECIFIC: any second custodian run on the same day loses that line, and `check_receipts` parses only `- HEAD:` so nothing anywhere notices. Filed as a sixth item against `custodian.sh` — author-key territory, so it queues to the M3 sitting beside D0152 item 3 and D0146 item 2, all three in the same file. . ARTIFACT 3 — AN EVIDENCE ROOT OUTSIDE `.gitignore`, WHICH WAS MINE. A hand pytest run during the assessment used `TANNEN_EVIDENCE_ROOT=.tannen-verify-evidence` — an invented name. `.gitignore:23` covers `.verify-evidence/` and nothing else, and step 9's `commit_with_hook_retry` does `git add -A`, so thirty-six evidence records rode into the sitting commit. Caught before any tag attested it, and removed at step 10's signing prompt — a moment when the driver is provably idle, blocked on `read` — with `git rm -r --cached` followed by `git commit --amend --no-verify`. Safe for four reasons, each checked rather than assumed: step 10 reads its DELEGATIONS and custody hashes from the WORKING TREE, which the amend does not touch; `git tag -s` resolves HEAD at signing time, after the amend; the attention receipt's recorded HEAD stayed an ancestor of the new commit; and no tag yet attested the old one. `git ls-tree -r HEAD` now returns zero such paths. . The `.gitignore` stanza above that line already argues this exact hazard — "a red gate leaves it behind, and the boundary sitting commits with `git add -A`". It names one path where the hazard is the pattern. The builder-side rule that follows: when running the suite by hand in this repo, use `.verify-evidence`, never an invented root. | accepted | — | governance-paths | file: `.gitignore`; file: `scripts/custodian.sh`; file: `scripts/check_receipts.py` |

| D0156 | A | A delta is a Rel over the same semiring — no Delta type — and delta-capability is declared per component, with B refused by name | A delta is a `Rel` over the same semiring as the relation it changes (docs/specs/m3.md §3.1). There is NO `Delta[K, S]` wrapper type. `Rel` already constructs negative ℤ counts — nothing in it inspects sign — the `rel/1` canonical form already encodes them, and the witnessed-row invariant (frozen L2.2/D0110) already does the right thing unprompted: `(-1, {{r}})` is accepted, `(-1, ∅)` refused. A retraction therefore owes provenance exactly as an arrival does, by a rule that already exists. . Delta-capability is DECLARED per component. A semiring is delta-capable when every component of its (possibly product) structure is either a GROUP component declaring `negate` with `add(a, negate(a)) == zero` law-checked where the other axioms are, or a `Why` component, for which `negate(w) = w` — `Why` is a join-semilattice under `add`, idempotent, no inverse. `Z` and `Z*Why` qualify; `B` declares no `negate` and every delta operation refuses it BY NAME. No M1 refusal lifts: `Z.multiplicity`/`collapse` still raise on a negative (§3.4 re-commissions those raises, D0158), so frozen L1.2 stays true by design. . REJECTED: a distinct `Delta[K, S]` type. It would double the operator surface — every bilinear rule would need `Rel × Δ`, `Δ × Rel` and `Δ × Δ` signatures — fork the store format, and contradict P4's one-annotated-relation-type principle. DBSP itself draws no such distinction: a delta is an element of the same abelian group as the state. The witnessed-row invariant already giving a retraction a provenance obligation is the tell that `Rel` was the right carrier all along. . REJECTED: guessing symmetric difference for `B` so it too could be delta-capable. A set semiring has no retractions; inventing one would be the silent coercion the door forbids (exactness-and-the-door). Refusing by name is the door working. | accepted | — | — | manifest: `docs/specs/m3.md`; manifest: `tests/laws/m3/test_l3_delta.py` |
| D0157 | A | apply's normalisation order is add → cone → group-zero drop → valuation, and byte identity is the L2–L4 equality — earned, not quotiented | `apply(base, delta, dead)` is pointwise addition followed by three normalisation steps IN THIS ORDER (docs/specs/m3.md §3.3): (1) the CONE CHECK — a row driven below the non-negative cone is an over-retraction, refused by name, which is where m1 §4.4's promised loud break lands, at the operation whose arguments made the question askable; (2) the GROUP-ZERO DROP — a row zero in every group component is dropped, `(0, {{r}})` included, because the reference has no such row; (3) the VALUATION — every surviving row's every `Why` is filtered by `surviving(w, dead)` (M2 §4, now kernel code). The criterion for step 2 is the group components, NOT the bag image: a positive count whose `Why` is empty must fall through to be refused by the witnessed-row invariant, never be dropped as bag-empty. Construction is untouched — a caller-built `(0, {{r}})` is still retained (frozen L1.4/D0093); `apply` is a new operation choosing what to EMIT. . L2, L3 and L4 assert CONTENT-ADDRESS equality — the same byte identity L1 gave replay and the golden corpus pins — not a quotient. For pure arrivals it is free: a `srcrow/1` ref depends on `(source, row)` only, so any partition unions identical refs idempotently while counts add commutatively. For retractions it is EARNED by step 3: `Why` is PosBool with no subtraction, so pointwise addition leaves the cumulative run's witnesses where the reference has the net run's, and `surviving(w, dead)` recovers the reference exactly on the positive fragment (the residue theorem, L3.11). `anti_join` sits outside that fragment and earns byte identity by replay instead (D0163's contagion rule). . REJECTED: equality up to bag image (a quotient). It states less than is true and silently abandons BRIEF §5.5's promise that the default pipeline's provenance survives a delta — L2.3 would become meaningless for any integral that ever saw a retraction. So the cone raises at `Z.multiplicity`, `Z.collapse` and `anti_join`'s presence test DO NOT EXPIRE. A semilattice cannot subtract, so apply-maintenance through `anti_join` is unsound; replaying is the honest rule, priced by BRIEF §10. The unsound variant is kept as the mutant `antijoin-delta-maintained`, and the `right-moves` perturbation stream draws the superseding-address case on purpose (D0118's rule paying for itself a second time). | D0167 | A | The delta executor's surface: code referenced by name, replay as a declared parameter, and the two trace properties advance INHERITS from M1 rather than invents | `tannen.incremental` is implemented at Session B against the surface frozen L3.15 pins (`DeltaNode`, `Ledger`/`Ledger.EMPTY`, `advance(...) -> .state_ref/.delta_ref/ .ledger_ref/.step_id/.rebuilt`). Five choices the spec left open, and two properties that need saying out loud because a reader will otherwise read them as bugs. . (1) CODE IS REFERENCED BY NAME. A `DeltaNode`'s descriptor is the content address of its declared form, and a lambda has no content address — a descriptor over one would be a lie. So `select` declares `predicate_id`, `map_rows` declares `map_id`, and `aggregate` declares `monoid_id` XOR `group_id`, each resolved out of a module-level registry (`PREDICATES`, `MAPS`, `MONOIDS`, `GROUPS`) with `register_*` for callers. The shipped registries are SEEDED with the M3 catalogue (`x-positive`, `k-only`, `sum`) because the frozen law files name those ids and the shipped package must resolve them. Re-registering a name with a different object is refused: a name a descriptor carries may not change meaning. Parameters are validated and the code they name resolved AT DECLARATION, not at the tick — a plan's mistakes should not wait for data to arrive to be found. . (2) `replay` IS A DECLARED PARAMETER, hence part of the descriptor. §4's contagion rule is a property of the caller's PLAN ("no `anti_join` at or below this node"), and the executor has no graph to compute it from (§7 declined one). So the caller declares it, and `distinct`/`aggregate`/`anti_join` replay whatever the caller says, because their rule is replacement regardless. . (3) FOUR VALUE TAGS: `deltaop/1` (the declared node), `incstate/1` (the node's integral refs — output always, inputs where the rule needs them: a `join` keeps both children's, a subtractive `aggregate` keeps its input's), `incstep/1` (what one step produced) and `ledger/1` (§6, spec-given). A column-set parameter is SORTED into the declared form, so two spellings of the same node are the same descriptor. . (4) THE TRACE IS CONSULTED, AND BY DEFAULT NOT WRITTEN; `record=True` is the caller's act. This is forced, and the force is worth recording: frozen `test_l3_15_a_tampered_trace_raises` calls `traces.record(done.step_id, <garbage>)` AFTER a successful `advance` and outside its `pytest.raises` block. `TraceStore.record` raises on a conflicting re-record, so if `advance` had recorded under `step_id` that line would raise and the frozen law would error rather than pass. The honest reading is that recording is a policy, exactly as M1 already makes it one between `AlwaysRebuild` and `VerifyingTrace`; `advance` takes the same choice as a flag, defaulting off. Consequently `rebuilt` reports whether this step's output was NEW TO THE STORE, not whether a function was called: everything a step produces is content-addressed, so a replay writes nothing and reports `rebuilt=False` whether or not a trace entry served it. §7's "replaying a stream hits traces" is therefore available (`record=True`) rather than automatic, which is a narrowing of the spec's prose and is queued for the M3 boundary sitting (D0154) as such. . (5) A NODE-LEVEL QUARANTINE IS UNREACHABLE FROM `advance`, and the guard stays. Its inputs are relations loaded from the store, never an upstream `Quarantine`, so only ROW-level quarantine can arise; those rows are stored and named by `quarantined_ref` — reports about a tick, never state (BRIEF P3) — and the integral simply lacks them. `Advanced.quarantine` is the P3 rule stated where it belongs, not a path this suite reaches. . INHERITED, NOT INVENTED: `step_id` is `derivation_id(descriptor, inputs)`, which m1 §8 defines as ORDER-INSENSITIVE in the inputs, and §7 pins that formula ("sorted delta refs"). So a binary node's operand order is not part of its step id, and `advance(node, None, [a, b])` and `advance(node, None, [b, a])` share a step id while computing different things. This is M1's own property — `Node(transform, inputs)` has it identically, since `f(a, b)` and `f(b, a)` share a derivation id there too — carried forward rather than quietly diverged from. It is pinned by a test that says so, it is the second reason `advance` does not record by default, and it is queued for the sitting alongside (4). | accepted | — | public-surface | file: `src/tannen/incremental.py`; manifest: `tests/laws/m3/test_l3_executor.py`; pytest: `tests/test_incremental.py::test_a_replayed_step_is_served_from_the_trace_when_the_caller_records`; pytest: `tests/test_incremental.py::test_a_binary_step_id_inherits_derivation_ids_order_insensitivity`; pytest: `tests/test_incremental.py::test_a_node_is_refused_at_declaration_not_at_the_tick`; pytest: `tests/test_incremental.py::test_the_contagion_rule_sheds_a_superseded_anti_join_address` |

The multi-slot case is refused by name before this runs (D0161), so "the" `Why` is well defined wherever the conjunction happens. . This record is not a second authorisation. It is the execution, the two things the execution turns out to cost that D0115 did not price, and the one question D0115 never asked. . OWNER RULINGS TAKEN 2026-09-06, in conversation, and queued here for signature the way D0115 itself was: (1) excise all 12 sibling snapshot files from history, not merely from the published tree; (2) licence the result Apache-2.0, superseding the MIT/CC-BY-SA-4.0 split in `policy.yaml licence_defaults` — which that file already says is a default and not a publication decision. . === WHY MECHANISM (a) IS NOT A REDACTION, MEASURED === . D0115 recommends keeping the snapshots and excluding them from the published tree. `concepts/snapshots/**` entered at the ROOT COMMIT `5c3a474` and has been touched in exactly one commit in the repository's life, so all 594 lines sit in the tree of every one of the 77 commits across all five branches. Deleting them at HEAD leaves them one `git show 5c3a474` away. And the history is what gets published: `.github/workflows/ ci.yml` pins `fetch-depth: 0` because the receipt chain asserts ancestry between recorded HEADs and the tag set is part of the custody floor. Mechanism (a) is still needed — it is what lets the registry verify once the bytes are gone — but it is the CONSEQUENCE of an excision, never a substitute for one. . === WHAT THE REWRITE COSTS, REHEARSED RATHER THAN ASSERTED === . `docs/proposals/2026-09-06-publication/rehearse_rewrite.sh`, 14 steps, in a disposable clone; the source repository was never written to. 77 commits in, 77 out, none dropped, a complete 77-pair `commit-map` with zero null entries. The 12 files are absent from every commit of every ref; `concepts/snapshots/semiring-relations/` — this project's excerpt of its own BRIEF — survives, which keeps `check_concepts.py`'s byte-verifying path non-vacuous in the published tree rather than leaving it a branch nothing takes. . ALL EIGHT TAGS: `object CHANGED / signature BROKEN`, measured, every one. That includes `brief-freeze`, whose TAG OBJECT hash `c219e63819beb4052b326e47b9cbd5d208779cda` is pinned at `governance/tag-roles.yaml#trust_root.object` — the file that calls re-issuing it "the one act that would otherwise redefine every other check in the custody floor", and which `check_tag_signers.py` exists to detect. This plan performs that act deliberately, under signature, with the old value preserved here. Re-creation works: the four builder tags were re-signed with the real builder key at their ORIGINAL tagger dates via `GIT_COMMITTER_DATE` and all four verify with dates unchanged, so `bless_epoch` and D0036's delegation-precedes-signature ordering are undisturbed. . === THE RECEIPTS ARE NOT RE-SIGNED, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN === . A rewrite kills all five: `check_receipts.py` runs `cat-file -e` on each recorded HEAD and every one becomes a non-commit. The obvious repair — edit each receipt to carry the new SHA and re-sign — fabricates an attestation of a moment nobody attested to, which is the precise thing the chain exists to prevent. Refused. . Instead the five receipts stay BYTE-IDENTICAL and the rewrite declares itself: `receipts/REWRITE-<date>.md`, owner-signed under its own namespace `tannen-rewrite` (distinct from `tannen-receipt` so neither signature can be replayed as the other), carrying the COMPLETE old->new map. `check_receipts.py` resolves each recorded HEAD through the map before looking it up. The chain then verifies end to end through a discontinuity that is itself signed, dated and public — which is strictly more than an un-rewritten history proves about itself. . Measured: against the rewritten history the shipped guard reports five "the history the owner attested to is gone" failures; with the patch and a signed attestation all five clear, with no receipt or receipt signature touched. Three negative controls, each watched going red per D0111/D0116 — attestation removed (the five failures return); attestation present but unsigned ("unsigned, it is the rewriting party vouching for itself"); attestation signed but map tampered (red twice, on the signature AND on the remapped commit being absent). And no regression: against the real un-rewritten tree the patched guard prints exactly what the shipped one prints. . === THE PIN COUNT, AND THE VACUITY IT CLOSES === . D0115 makes one condition non-optional: a degraded `check_concepts.py` must COUNT the pins it verified against an expectation not derived from the files it is checking, or publication installs species I of D0116's taxonomy inside its own publication door. The expectation goes in `governance/policy.yaml` (`concept_registry.expected_citation_pins: 13`) — owner-signed, in `required_signatures`, and not a file the degraded path also skips. Thirteen is measured: 13 `snapshot.path` entries across 8 records, all unique. Eight probes, all run: baseline 13-by-bytes green; one snapshot absent -> 12+1 green; the PUBLISHED configuration (all 12 gone) -> 1+12 green where the shipped guard reports 12 failures; then a concept record truncated away (11 != 13), the expectation key deleted, `policy.yaml` deleted outright, and `concepts/` emptied — all four RED. The shipped poison fixture still fails and still carries its marker. . === WHAT EXCISION DOES NOT REMOVE — THE QUESTION D0115 NEVER ASKED === . The plan this executes carried an acceptance test `git log --all -p -S 'renavon' -- concepts/` -> empty. The rehearsal falsified it, and the correction is the most useful thing this record carries. The borrowed TEXT goes; the CITATIONS stay, because they are what BRIEF §2 is for. A public reader still learns from `concepts/*.yaml`: four repository URLs including `renavondata/renavon-monorepo`; nine document paths including `docs/architecture/decisions/002-pipeline-rigour-stance.md`; section titles quoted verbatim, the renavon row's being an internal ADR heading; five pinned commit SHAs of private repositories. And `BRIEF.md` — frozen at `brief-freeze`, constitutional, unamendable — names all four in its §1 constellation table and describes the last as "The business; funds and supplies the empirical substrate". . So the owner's ruling answered "may this repo quote 58 lines of that ADR" and the remaining question is "may this repo NAME that repository, its ADR path and its section heading in public". They are different questions and only the first was put. If the answer to the second is also no, the renavon `source` entry leaves `concepts/provenance-ref-grammar.yaml`, `expected_citation_pins` becomes 12, the concept keeps its pkm source and stays `S-pending`, and the registry loses one of the two owners BRIEF §2 names for that row — a weakening of the citation discipline, not a tidy-up. It is queued as part of this record rather than guessed at. . === ALSO CORRECTED HERE, BECAUSE D0045 MAKES D0115 IMMUTABLE === . D0115 binds `governance/policy.yaml#external_surface.publishing` with `strength: enforced`. Measured at `5f206cc`: that key is read by NOTHING. It appears in prose and in the `check-manifest-unsigned-policy` poison fixture, nowhere in any guard. Its owner signature makes the clause unforgeable; no guard consults it before bytes leave. The binding should read `documentary`. And per D0175 the home-path disclosure count D0115 shows the owner is five, not four. . === STAGED, NOT APPLIED === .
